messages.author: 331b448e313706ec
messages.subject: save.lvs troubles
parts:
Hi there,

I'm running a fairly elaborate SEM model with a number of latent/factor variables. 

I've been trying to use the save.lvs = T option to work with the factor scores post-estimation. However, the blavaan call stops in the posterior check stage, with the simple output "Killed"

I tried increasing my RAM (I'm on a virtual machine and get more resources). As a result of that, got an error that some exports were too large, so I am using this option:
options(future.globals.maxSize = 4 * 1024^3). Now I am back to the process being "Killed" when doing posterior checks.

Some way I can debug this? Maybe save a log somewhere? Or calculate factor scores from the posterior (I am not sure why they would impact the posterior check?)

Thanks for your help.
PS: I am on blavaan 0.3-11.646 using the following call. I can show you the output without the "save.lvs" option if you like.

seed = 42156
fit = bcfa(
    model, 
    data = data.final,
    cp = 'srs',
    bcontrol = list(cores=4),
    n.chains=3, 
    burnin=2000, 
    sample = 4000,
    save.lvs = T,
    seed=seed
)

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: save.lvs troubles
parts:
Hi

A few quick recommnedations.
- Update blavaan, the current version is 0.3-12
- Run it in only 1 core, no parallel, in case there is an issue of how the virtual machine is communicating with R
- Save less samples. now you are saving 4000 samples per chain. Ig you have a large sample with a large model, your output objects might be too large with 12000. Probably 1000 would be enough. This might solve the
- If in this stage you are not interested in model fit use the argument test="none" so it doesnt doesnt estimate posterior checks. You can turn this off for the model without save.lvs=T (this will also make your output object smaller)
- blavaan suggest to use future::plan("multiprocess") to speed up post-MCMC computing. But if this is te stage that gives problems, might want to not call the future package and see if the error still happens. This because I think this error is refering the future functionality  :  options(future.globals.maxSize = 4 * 1024^3)

If this is doesnt work. Please post your model syntax and output

-- Mauricio
